findings.reason: src/diff/json.ts:100 now checks only `obj && obj.toJSON`, and line 101 then calls `obj.toJSON()`. A non-function truthy toJSON such as a string therefore throws a TypeError, while the old typeof-function guard (and JSON.stringify) treat it as an ordinary key.
findings.claim: diffJson/canonicalize throws a TypeError on objects that have a truthy toJSON property that is not a function.
findings.evidence: The diff changes `if (obj && typeof obj.toJSON === 'function')` to `if (obj && obj.toJSON)`, and the next line calls `obj = obj.toJSON();` unconditionally. A string, number or object value there is not callable, so the call throws. JSON.stringify only calls toJSON when it is a function, so the old guard matched the JSON semantics this function relies on.
